items.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026
items.q: So I went back and said hello. We all hung out, we had a nice little hang there.

ctx.x: Yeah, yes, yes. I do have memories of Joe Williams. I loved his whole style, his way of being on stage. I mean yeah he was something else. And see when I was coming up as a musician my mother always said, “You know I hope you get to –” she said her favorite singer was Joe Williams. So she was saying she would hope that maybe I would get to play with him someday, or know him or something like that. Or you know get to check him out live or something. So my mother was visiting me in New York and it happened

that Joe Williams was playing at a club there. So I said, “Hey Mom, we’re going out tonight.” And then she said, “Well where are we going?” I said, “You don’t worry about it,” you know, “just come on.” And then as we are getting ready she said, “Oh where is he playing?” She knew that that must have been why I was taking her out. So I said, “Yeah, okay you got it.” So I tipped the maître d – I guess he wouldn’t have been maître d – the waiter or the guy who met us there because – was it a restaurant? Yeah, maybe.…

Indeed. He was a classy guy. And he also was a good example, I’ve noticed with, I mentioned Joe Wilder, and Milt Hinton, they all had this thing that they were wonderful people, friendly. But at the same time they had so much pride in what they did, like don’t mess with that. Don’t disrespect what they do or you’ll be sorry. I mean they would react to something where they were being taken advantage of. They weren’t the kind of people that were just so nice that you could do anything and take advantage of them.…
